primitives.name: Goal Differential Adjusted Plus-Minus
primitives.verbatim_quote: The authors build (a) a regularized adjusted plus-minus on goal differential, (b) an expected-goals plus-minus (xGPM) with net xG per segment as target, and (c) an expected-points plus-minus (xPPM) using changes in in-play expected points as the target — then use them to rank European players and leagues.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the paper lies in adapting the plus-minus paradigm from basketball and hockey to soccer, addressing its unique challenges: low-scoring nature and long lineup segments. The authors propose three variants—goal-differential APM, xG APM, and xP APM—each targeting different aspects of performance. These are estimated using ridge regression to handle collinearity among players in fixed-lineup segments. Time decay weights and situational dummies enhance realism. The methodological novelty resides in applying these tools to soccer’s discrete event structure, where each segment represents a fixed set of players on the pitch. The key mathematical innovation is the use of a generalized linear model with group penalties, ensuring that correlated players (e.g., center-backs) share credit equally. This approach avoids the overfitting issues common in sparse data settings typical of soccer analytics. The failure mode occurs when the xG/xP models themselves are inaccurate or when the assumption of fixed lineups breaks down due to frequent substitutions or red cards. The empirical validation through ordered probit models ensures robustness but introduces potential leakage if the same data is used for both training and validation. The extension to NFL context hinges on translating these concepts to snap-level on/off splits, leveraging existing EPA frameworks while preserving the core structure of player attribution.
